digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate evidence attestation and credential grounding
propositions: Four gate escapes in epic 061c-ecd1 share a root cause: green signals whose measurement context (environment, principal, privilege posture, instrument type) was never recorded, making it impossible to verify whether the measurement could have observed the failure it claims to rule out

Escape 2b demonstrates that both a live call under wildcard identity and a policy simulator can produce confident but wrong or non-falsifiable evidence: the wildcard identity cannot fail at all, and the simulator answers the policy-language question rather than which action the service actually checks

No gate audits the measurement's context (account, region, privilege level, instrument type) against repo-grounded project state, and by design they cannot — plan-review runs before evidence exists and the completion-verifier is designed to trust operator attestations

A deterministic floor check must force measurement provenance (environment, principal, privilege_posture, instrument) into attested-evidence records as greppable text, enabling repo-grounded criteria to detect contradictions between a claim's stated measurement context and project facts

Plans asserting unchanged behavior across provider/route/model swaps while citing only configuration (no resolution path) are invisible to review because citation discipline creates a camouflage of virtue, allowing four-hop runtime dependencies to escape unexamined

The completion-verifier must NOT re-run world measurements to validate provenance, as its own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem; instead, provenance-as-text enables existing criteria to spot context contradictions
